title: Interactive Data Visualization in R with Shiny
text:
Learning Objectives


Articulate basic principles of interactive data visualization
Understand critical concepts from R-Shiny including the structure of a Shiny App, how to run a Shiny App, how to configure the aesthetics of a Shiny App, and how the reactive programming model of Shiny works.
Be able to augment a barebones Shiny app framework to develop a fully functioning Shiny app using provided data. This will encompass R and HTML programming.
Be able to identify tools and resources for sharing and deploying a Shiny app. Be aware of advanced style configuration using CSS.

title: Interactive Data Visualization in R with Shiny
text:
Welcome to Interactive Data Visualization in R with Shiny. This is a step-by-step guide walking through the code we will write together during our hands-on session.


Let’s begin by building the simplest Shiny application we can.

Create minimum skeleton for a Shiny app. Name file app.R to have it recognized as a shiny application.
Add a title to the page_sidebar labeled "Hello World!".


library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "Hello, world!"
)

server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

In this step-by-step lesson, we will create a simple Shiny application. To see the application we will be building, you can run:

library(shiny)
runExample("01_hello")





library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- page_sidebar(
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {
  
}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----

  # App title ----
  title = "Hello Shiny"
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)





library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----

  # App title ----
  title = "Hello Shiny",

  sidebar = sidebar()
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)





library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title ----
  title = "Hello Shiny",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    # Input: Slider for the number of bins ----

    sliderInput(
      inputId = "bins",
      label = "Number of bins:",
      min = 1,
      max = 50,
      value = 30
    )
  )
)

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)





library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- page_sidebar(# App title ----
                   title = "Hello Shiny", sidebar = sidebar(
                     # Input: Slider for the number of bins ----
                     
                     sliderInput(
                       inputId = "bins",
                       label = "Number of bins:",
                       min = 1,
                       max = 50,
                       value = 30
                     )))

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    x <- faithful$waiting
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
    
    hist(
      x,
      breaks = bins,
      col = "#75AADB",
      border = "white",
      xlab = "Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)",
      main = "Histogram of waiting times"
    )
  })
}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- page_sidebar(# App title ----

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----

  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    x <- faithful$waiting
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
    
    hist(
      x,
      breaks = bins,
      col = "#75AADB",
      border = "white",

# Create Shiny app ----

library(shiny)
library(bslib)

# Define UI for app that draws a histogram ----
ui <- page_sidebar(# App title ----
                   title = "Hello Shiny", sidebar = sidebar(
                     # Input: Slider for the number of bins ----
                     
                     sliderInput(
                       inputId = "bins",
                       label = "Number of bins:",
                       min = 1,
                       max = 50,
                       value = 30
                     )),
                    plotOutput("distPlot"),
      # Output: Eruptions Histogram
      plotOutput(outputId = "distPlotEruptions")
                   )

# Define server logic required to draw a histogram ----
server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
    x <- faithful$waiting
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
    
    hist(
      x,
      breaks = bins,
      col = "#75AADB",
      border = "white",
      xlab = "Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)",
      main = "Histogram of waiting times"
    )
  })
  
  
  output$distPlotEruptions <- renderPlot({
    
    x    <- faithful$eruptions
    bins <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = input$bins + 1)
    
    hist(x, breaks = bins, col = "#75AADB", border = "white",
         xlab = "Length of eruption (in mins)",
         main = "Histogram of eruption times")
    
  })
}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Interactive Data Visualization in R with Shiny
text:
We are going to apply the principles we learned on Day 1 to create a full-featured dashboard, and surface and address some concerns that arise as we do.


Just like our Day 1 example, we need to create a basic skeleton for our app, which includes:

Package imports (shiny and bslib are both dependencies for Shiny apps)
ui: The user interface layout (what the user sees)
server: The server runs our code, and reacts to changes from the user
shinyApp: Combines the two parts of our app (ui and server) and runs a local webserver to display our app in a browser.


library(shiny)
library(bslib)


ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard'
 
  )


server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




Here we load in our data that we will use in our dashboard. We will be using the palmerpenguins dataset.

We do a little data cleaning here:

Remove missing values with na.omit
Rename the column names with formatted, human readable titles


library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)

# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 



ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard'
 
  )


server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




Now let’s start developing our dashboard.
Let’s add a description of our data on the dashboard toinform the user what data is being displayed, and from where.
We add a sidebar where we will put our informational description, as well as our user input interactive elements.
Inside our sidebar we are adding a few things:

Text, which is indicated by "This application uses data from ..."
Code, which is formatted text, indicated by: code('palmerpenguins')
Image, which is added to our dashboard using the img function


library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)

# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 



ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  
  # Sidebar for user inputs
  sidebar = sidebar(
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    # Code snippet
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    # Display image (works with url to image as well)
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    "Artwork by @allison_horst"
  )
)


server <- function(input, output) {
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




Now let’s create a simple scatterplot visualization of our penguins:

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)
# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 



ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  
  # Sidebar for user inputs
  sidebar = sidebar(
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    # Code snippet
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    # Display image (works with url to image as well)
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    p("Artwork by @allison_horst")
  ),
  
  
  card(card_header("Scatterplot"), 
       plotOutput("scatterplot")),
  
)


server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
    
    ggplot(penguins,
           aes(x = `Bill Length (mm)`,
               y = `Bill Depth (mm)`,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




Right now our data visualization is static. If we want to make it interactive, we need to first create some inputs that the users can control, that are related to our data visualization.
Since our visualization uses the arguments for the x (Bill Length (mm)) and y (Bill Depth (mm)) axes, we will create a selector that allows the user to choose alternative x and y variables.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)

# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 



ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  sidebar = sidebar(
 
    # List selector based on the columns in a dataframe 
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = 'xvar', 
      label = 'X variable',
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Length (mm)'
    ),
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = "yvar", 
      label = "Y variable",
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Depth (mm)'
    ),
    
    # Visual line divider
    hr(), 
    
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    "Artwork by @allison_horst"),
  
  
  card(card_header("Scatterplot"),
       plotOutput("scatterplot")),
 
  )


server <- function(input, output) {
  
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
    
    ggplot(penguins,
           # Coerce a string to a literal using the !! prefix
           aes(x = !!input$xvar,
               y = !!input$yvar,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




We also want to add a way for the user to select specific penguins species to explore in the dashboard, which we do with a checkboxGroupInput.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)

# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 



ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  sidebar = sidebar(
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = 'xvar', 
      label = 'X variable',
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Length (mm)'
    ),
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = "yvar", 
      label = "Y variable",
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Depth (mm)'
    ),

    # Checkbox selector - returns a vector of strings, length 0, 1, 
    # 2, or 3, depending on the number of species selected
    checkboxGroupInput(
      inputId = "species",
      label = "Select Penguin Species",
      choices = c("Adelie" = "Adelie",
                  "Chinstrap" = "Chinstrap",
                  "Gentoo" = "Gentoo"),
      selected = c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
    ),
    
    hr(), 
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    p("Artwork by @allison_horst")),
  
  
  card(card_header("Scatterplot"),
       plotOutput("scatterplot")),
 
  )


server <- function(input, output) {
  
 # Reactive function - returns a filtered dataframe
 penguins_filter <- reactive({
   req(input$species)
   penguins |> dplyr::filter(Species %in% input$species)
 })
 
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
    
    ggplot(penguins_filter(),
           aes(x = !!input$xvar,
               y = !!input$yvar,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)




When we choose different species, we want to ensure they are represented with consistent colors across all visualizations. We explictly assign colors, specifically colorblind friendly colors, using RColorBrewer.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)
# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 

# Display all qualitative colors
# display.brewer.all(type = "qual")

# Create a colorblind friendly qualitative palette
color_blind_palette <- brewer.pal(3, "Dark2") 
# Match colors to species names
names(color_blind_palette) <-  c("Gentoo", "Adelie", "Chinstrap")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  sidebar = sidebar(
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = 'xvar', 
      label = 'X variable',
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Length (mm)'
    ),
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = "yvar", 
      label = "Y variable",
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Depth (mm)'
    ),
    
    checkboxGroupInput(
      inputId = "species",
      label = "Select Penguin Species",
      choices = c("Adelie" = "Adelie",
                  "Chinstrap" = "Chinstrap",
                  "Gentoo" = "Gentoo"),
      selected = c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
    ),
    
    hr(), 
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    p("Artwork by @allison_horst")),
  
  
  card(card_header("Scatterplot"),
       plotOutput("scatterplot")),
 
  )


server <- function(input, output) {
  
  
 penguins_filter <- reactive({
   req(input$species)
   penguins |> dplyr::filter(Species %in% input$species)
 })
 
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
    
    ggplot(penguins_filter(),
           aes(x = !!input$xvar,
               y = !!input$yvar,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      # Apply the manual color palette
      scale_color_manual(values = color_blind_palette) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

The minimum and maximum range in the x-axis and y-axis is determined by our data. If we are only looking at one species, rather than all species, we may have a different minimum and maximum. This means it’s difficult to draw valid comparisons between different subsets of our data.




library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# load data
data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)
# rename the columns for clarity in app
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 

#display.brewer.all(type = "qual")
color_blind_palette <- brewer.pal(3, "Dark2") 
names(color_blind_palette) <-  c("Gentoo", "Adelie", "Chinstrap")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard',
  sidebar = sidebar(
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = 'xvar', 
      label = 'X variable',
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),

in a conditional statement that will only enable it if the conditional evaluates as TRUE (the user has selected it using a checkbox):

    ),

server <- function(input, output) {
  
  
 penguins_filter <- reactive({
   req(input$species)
   penguins |> dplyr::filter(Species %in% input$species)
 })
 
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
    
    ggplot(penguins_filter(),
           aes(x = !!input$xvar,
               y = !!input$yvar,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      # Enable geom and facet_wrap if input$value is TRUE
      {if (input$smoother) geom_smooth()} +
      {if (input$facet) facet_wrap(vars(Island))} +
      xlim(c(min(penguins[input$xvar]), 
             max(penguins[input$xvar]))) +
      ylim(c(min(penguins[input$yvar]), 
             max(penguins[input$yvar]))) +
      scale_color_manual(values = color_blind_palette) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

title: Interactive Data Visualization in R with Shiny
text:
Finally, we will output summary statistics for our user’s data selection, along with a display of the filtered dataframe.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(RColorBrewer)

data(penguins, package = "palmerpenguins")

# remove missing values, in any row
penguins <- na.omit(penguins)
colnames(penguins) <- c("Species",
                        "Island",
                        "Bill Length (mm)",
                        "Bill Depth (mm)",
                        "Flipper Length (mm)",
                        "Body Mass (g)",
                        "Sex",
                        "Year") 

# Custom color palette
color_blind_palette <- brewer.pal(3, "Dark2") 
names(color_blind_palette) <-  c("Gentoo", "Adelie", "Chinstrap")

ui <- page_sidebar(
  # App title
  title = 'Palmer Penguin Dashboard', 
  
  #Sidebar panel for inputs
  sidebar = sidebar(
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = 'xvar', 
      label = 'X variable',
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Length (mm)'
    ),
    
    varSelectInput(
      inputId = "yvar", 
      label = "Y variable",
      data = dplyr::select(penguins, where(is.numeric), -Year),
      selected = 'Bill Depth (mm)'
    ),
  
    checkboxGroupInput(
      inputId = "species",
      label = "Select Penguin Species",
      choices = c("Adelie" = "Adelie",
                  "Chinstrap" = "Chinstrap",
                  "Gentoo" = "Gentoo"),
      selected = c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo")
    ),
   
    checkboxInput(inputId ="smoother", 
                  label = "Add smoother",
                  value= FALSE),
    
    checkboxInput(inputId ="facet", 
                  label = "Add facet by island",
                  value= FALSE),
    hr(), 
    "This application uses data from the package:",
    code('palmerpenguins'),
    img(src = 'penguins.png'),
    p("Artwork by @allison_horst")),
  
  card(card_header("Scatterplot"),
       plotOutput("scatterplot")),
  
  # Create a side by side layout for summary and table outputs
  layout_columns(
    card(card_header("Summary"),
       verbatimTextOutput("summary")),
    card(card_header("Dataframe"),
         tableOutput("table"),
         # Control the maximum height a card can take. Syntax 
         # derives from CSS.
         max_height = "400px"),
    # Control the width of each column. Values sum to 12, so
    # a value of c(3,9) would mean column 2 would be 3 times as 
    # wide as column 1
    col_widths = c(5.5,6.5)
  )
  
  
  
  )

  
display.brewer.all(type = "qual")
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
 penguins_filter <- reactive({
   req(input$species)
   penguins |> dplyr::filter(Species %in% input$species)
 })
 # Use aes_string to pass the variables programmatically 
 # - they are returned from varSelectInput as strings
  output$scatterplot <- renderPlot({
    
 # character and literal values in aes   
    penguins_filter <- penguins |> dplyr::filter(Species %in% input$species)
    
    ggplot(penguins_filter(),
           aes(x = !!input$xvar,
               y = !!input$yvar,
               color = Species)) +
      geom_point(size = 5,
                 alpha = 0.5) +
      {if (input$smoother) geom_smooth()} +
      {if (input$facet) facet_wrap(vars(Island))} +
      xlim(c(min(penguins[input$xvar]), 
             max(penguins[input$xvar]))) +
      ylim(c(min(penguins[input$yvar]), 
             max(penguins[input$yvar]))) +
      scale_color_manual(values = color_blind_palette) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
      theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  })

  # Create output statistical summary of filtered dataframe  
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    summary(penguins_filter())
  })

  # Create output table to display filtered dataframe in app 
  output$table <- renderTable(penguins_filter()) 
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
